symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Number of endogenous variables.

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: Number of observed environment slots.

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: Maximum number of arbitrarily replaced covariance slots.

symbols.name: E
symbols.def: Set of observed environment labels.

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: Unknown honest set with \(\lvert H\rvert=h\).

symbols.name: PSDp
symbols.def: Cone of real symmetric positive-semidefinite \(p\times p\) matrices.

symbols.name: SPDp
symbols.def: Cone of real symmetric positive-definite \(p\times p\) matrices.

symbols.name: Sigma
symbols.def: Observed population covariance family \(\Sigma=(\Sigma_e:e\in E)\), with every honest or replaced slot chosen from the positive-semidefinite covariance domain.

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: Structural demixing matrix in the equilibrium equation.

symbols.name: H1
symbols.def: Fitted slot set of the first competing BACKSHIFT explanation, with \(\lvert H_1\rvert\ge h\).

symbols.name: H2
symbols.def: Fitted slot set of the second competing BACKSHIFT explanation, with \(\lvert H_2\rvert\ge h\).

symbols.name: J
symbols.def: Overlap \(J=H_1\cap H_2\) of the two fitted slot sets.
symbols.role: Common slots used by the overlap lemma.

symbols.name: D1
symbols.def: Structural matrix \(D^{(1)}\) in the first competing explanation.

symbols.name: D2
symbols.def: Structural matrix \(D^{(2)}\) in the second competing explanation.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Connectivity matrix \(B=I_p-D\).
symbols.role: Causal connectivity target reported by BACKSHIFT.

symbols.name: CP
symbols.def: Maximum absolute product along a directed simple cycle of length at least two.

symbols.name: Dcal
symbols.def: Matrix set satisfying the BACKSHIFT unit-diagonal and cycle-product normalization defined in \(\text{def:admissible-matrices}\).

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: Invariant disturbance covariance, permitted to be nondiagonal.

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: Honest intervention-variance levels \(s=(s_{ek}:e\in H,1\le k\le p)\).

symbols.name: s1
symbols.def: Shift levels \(s^{(1)}=(s^{(1)}_{ek}:e\in H_1,1\le k\le p)\) in the first competing explanation.
symbols.role: First explanation's shifts on the overlap.

symbols.name: s2
symbols.def: Shift levels \(s^{(2)}=(s^{(2)}_{ek}:e\in H_2,1\le k\le p)\) in the second competing explanation.
symbols.role: Second explanation's shifts on the overlap.

symbols.name: L
symbols.space: \(\{L:L\text{ is an affine line in }\mathbb R^2\}\)
symbols.def: Generic affine line used to measure concentration of a pairwise shift cloud.

symbols.name: Mkl
symbols.def: Maximum affine-line occupancy \(M_{k\ell}=\max_L\#\{e\in H:(s_{ek},s_{e\ell})\in L\}\).

symbols.name: delta
symbols.def: Environment deletion distance \(\delta_H=\min_{1\le k<\ell\le p}(h-M_{k\ell})\).

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: Proposal-specific prespecified support pattern for shift amplitudes.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: Random positive amplitudes indexed by the honest environment and coordinate.

symbols.name: Mgen
symbols.def: Generic occupancy formula \(M_{k\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}=\max\{n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell},n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{01}^{k\ell},n_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},\min(2,h)\}\).

symbols.name: Rc
symbols.def: Population \(c\)-replacement compatibility set defined in \(\text{def:compatible-set}\).
symbols.role: Recovery map for the structural target.

symbols.name: SubsetConsensus
symbols.def: Finite reduction of \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\) to exact feasibility-oracle queries over subsets of size \(h\), defined in \(\text{def:subset-consensus}\).
symbols.role: Definitional computational interface, not a supplied terminating solver.

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.def: Worst-overlap affine-minor separation, equal to zero when \(h-c<3\) and otherwise \(\gamma_H=\min_{k<\ell}\min_{S\subseteq H,\,|S|=h-c}\max_{e<f<g\in S}|\det[(1,s_{rk},s_{r\ell})_{r\in\{e,f,g\}}]|\).

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.def: Condition number \(\kappa_D=\|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|D^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).

symbols.name: zeta
symbols.def: Cycle-product normalization slack \(\zeta_D=1-\operatorname{CP}(I_p-D)\).

symbols.name: Mbound
symbols.def: Operator-norm scale bound \(M_H=1+\|\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in H}\|\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in H}\|\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: Common within-environment sample-size index.
symbols.role: Asymptotic index for the inference layer.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: Nominal noncoverage probability.

symbols.name: diamOp
symbols.def: Operator-norm diameter of a nonempty matrix set.
symbols.role: Size of a set-valued structural output.

symbols.name: outerOp
symbols.def: Operator-norm outer radius of a nonempty matrix set around \(D\).
symbols.role: One-sided contraction criterion for the confidence union.

symbols.name: gamma0
symbols.def: Fixed rational lower bound \(\gamma_0\) for the true honest-design affine-minor separation.

symbols.name: zeta0
symbols.def: Fixed rational lower bound \(\zeta_0\) for the true structural matrix's cycle-product normalization slack.

symbols.name: kappabar
symbols.def: Fixed rational upper bound \(\overline\kappa\) for the true and every feasible-candidate structural condition number.
symbols.role: Declarative true-side and candidate-side uniform conditioning bound.

symbols.name: Mbar
symbols.def: Fixed rational upper bound \(\overline M\) for the true honest-design scale functional.

symbols.name: Calpha
symbols.type: indexed nonempty random positive-semidefinite matrix-region family
symbols.def: Nonempty simultaneous covariance regions \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{\alpha}=(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}:e\in E)\), with each \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\subseteq\mathbb S_{+}^p\) arbitrary and nonempty.

symbols.name: rRadius
symbols.def: Honest-slot simultaneous operator-norm radius \(r_{n,\alpha,H}=\max_{e\in H}\sup_{\Gamma\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}}\|\Gamma-\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), with value \(+\infty\) allowed.
symbols.role: Observable-region error radius around the honest population covariances.

symbols.name: Ualpha
symbols.def: Indexed set-theoretic confidence union \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}\) defined in \(\text{def:confidence-union}\).
symbols.role: Set-valued compatibility functional and identification-robust confidence union.

assumptions.condition: \(s_{ek}\ge0\) for every \(e\in H\) and \(1\le k\le p\).

standard.name: Population BACKSHIFT covariance equation, with the invariant-noise cone stated separately.

assumptions.condition: \(s_{ek}=Z_{ek}a_{ek}\) for every \(e\in H\) and \(1\le k\le p\).

novel.justification: The prespecified-support factorization is a proposal-specific restriction that conditions on an investigator-chosen sparse intervention design. It is realistic in multi-environment experiments whose intervention targets are fixed before continuously distributed positive doses are assigned.

assumptions.condition: The joint law of \((a_{ek}:e\in H,1\le k\le p,Z_{ek}=1)\) is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on its positive orthant.

novel.justification: Joint absolute continuity conditional on a fixed sparse support pattern is a genericity condition for nonzero intervention strengths. It is satisfied when active intervention variances have a joint density on the positive orthant, including independently randomized positive strengths and correlated continuously distributed dose designs.

definitions.name: Mkl
definitions.construction: For \(1\le k<\ell\le p\), \(M_{k\ell}=\max_{L\subset\mathbb R^2\,\mathrm{affine\ line}}\#\{e\in H:(s_{ek},s_{e\ell})\in L\}\).

definitions.name: Rc
definitions.construction: For \(\Sigma\in(\mathbb S_{+}^{p})^{E}\), \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{A\in\mathcal D:\exists K\subseteq E,\ |K|\ge h,\ \exists\Psi\in\mathbb S_{+}^p,\ \exists t_e\in[0,\infty)^p,\ \Sigma_e=A^{-1}(\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e))A^{-\mathsf T}\ \forall e\in K\}\).

definitions.name: gamma
definitions.construction: Set \(\gamma_H=0\) when \(h-c<3\); otherwise set \(\gamma_H=\min_{1\le k<\ell\le p}\min_{S\subseteq H,\,|S|=h-c}\max_{e<f<g\in S}\left|\det\begin{pmatrix}1&s_{ek}&s_{e\ell}\\1&s_{fk}&s_{f\ell}\\1&s_{gk}&s_{g\ell}\end{pmatrix}\right|\).

definitions.name: SubsetConsensus
definitions.construction: Definitional implementation note: given a feasibility oracle that returns the full solution set for each queried semialgebraic system, query every \(K\subseteq E\) with \(|K|=h\) for all \(A\in\mathcal D\) satisfying \(\operatorname{offdiag}(A(\Sigma_e-\Sigma_f)A^{\mathsf T})=0\) for \(e,f\in K\) and admitting one \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_{+}^p\) with nonnegative diagonal shifts for the transformed raw covariances. Define \(\text{SubsetConsensus}(\Sigma,c)\) as the union of the oracle-returned solution sets. This enumeration makes exactly \(\binom{m}{h}\) oracle queries and, by expansion of \(\text{def:compatible-set}\), its returned union equals \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\); neither fact is a theorem contribution or a claim that an encoded terminating solver is supplied.

definitions.name: rRadius
definitions.construction: \(r_{n,\alpha,H}=\max_{e\in H}\sup_{\Gamma\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}}\|\Gamma-\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}\in[0,+\infty]\), where the supremum and hence the maximum may equal \(+\infty\).

definitions.name: diamOp
definitions.construction: For every nonempty matrix set \(\mathcal A\), \(\operatorname{diam}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal A)=\sup_{A_1,A_2\in\mathcal A}\|A_1-A_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}\in[0,+\infty]\).

definitions.name: outerOp
definitions.construction: For every nonempty matrix set \(\mathcal A\) and matrix \(D\), \(\operatorname{outer}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal A,D)=\sup_{A_1\in\mathcal A}\|A_1-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\in[0,+\infty]\).

definitions.name: Ualpha
definitions.construction:
For every \(n\geq1\), \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and indexed family of nonempty sets \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\subseteq\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\), define the set-theoretic confidence union
\[
\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}
=\bigcup_{\Gamma\in\prod_{e\in E}\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}}
\mathcal R_c(\Gamma).
\]
Thus \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}\) is the union of the population replacement-compatibility sets over all simultaneous selections from the covariance regions. This definition asserts neither computability nor a coverage property.

statements.statement: Let the first explanation \(D^{(1)},H_1,s^{(1)}\) and the second explanation \(D^{(2)},H_2,s^{(2)}\) fit the same \(\Sigma\), each through a BACKSHIFT covariance equation satisfying the unit-diagonal and cycle-product normalization, with its own invariant positive-semidefinite nuisance, nonnegative shifts, and \(|H_r|\ge h=m-c\). Set \(J=H_1\cap H_2\). Then \(|J|\ge m-2c=h-c\). If, for every \(k<\ell\), the first explanation's cloud \(\{(s^{(1)}_{ek},s^{(1)}_{e\ell}):e\in J\}\) is not contained in an affine line, then \(D^{(1)}=D^{(2)}\).
statements.justification: This isolates the new robust step: competing explanations share only \(m-2c\) slots, on which ordinary congruence-diagonalizer uniqueness must be normalized causally.
statements.gap: RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Theorem 1, and KleinsteuberShen2013NUJDUniqueness, Theorem 1, treat a fixed complete diagonalizable family rather than the intersection of two adversarially selected families.
statements.consumer: The lemma supplies the sufficiency half of the exact replacement-radius theorem after two candidate honest sets lose different slots.

statements.statement: Fix an honest BACKSHIFT instance \(D,H,s,\Omega\) with \(D\in\mathcal D\), nonnegative shifts, \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\), and \(\Sigma_e=D^{-1}(\Omega+\operatorname{diag}(s_e))D^{-\mathsf T}\) for every \(e\in H\). If \(\delta_H>c\), equivalently \(\gamma_H>0\), then \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) for every assignment of matrices in \(\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\) to the \(c\) slots in \(E\setminus H\). If, in addition, this fixed instance has \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\) and \(\delta_H\le c\), then there are positive-definite values for all slots in \(E\setminus H\), a matrix \(D'\in\mathcal D\) with \(D'\ne D\), an invariant \(\Omega'\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\), and nonnegative shifts on a set \(H'\subseteq E\) with \(|H'|=h\) such that \(D,D'\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\). Consequently, over the published class allowing \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\) and positive-semidefinite covariance slots, the threshold \(\delta_H>c\) is minimax sharp: whenever \(\delta_H\le c\), the class contains an ambiguity witness in its positive-definite invariant-noise and covariance subclass. No ambiguity is asserted for every fixed singular boundary value of \(\Omega\). On the positive-definite invariant-noise interior and at \(c=0\), the equivalence is exactly the BACKSHIFT pairwise noncollinearity criterion.
statements.justification: The theorem gives full published-class sufficiency and the exact minimax number of whole covariance environments that population BACKSHIFT can lose, with pointwise necessity stated only where its interior deformation is valid.
statements.gap: Published BACKSHIFT gives the all-honest criterion, while threshold-trimming joint diagonalization does not provide a worst-case whole-slot replacement radius, a legal contamination, or the distinction between boundary sufficiency and interior pointwise necessity.
statements.consumer: Investigators obtain an exact design audit: passing the distance test certifies every positive-semidefinite covariance assignment, while failing it rules out a uniform class guarantee through an explicit positive-definite ambiguity witness.

statements.statement: Under the prespecified support pattern \(Z\) and absolutely continuous active amplitudes, simultaneously for every \(k<\ell\), \(M_{k\ell}=M_{k\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\) almost surely. Consequently, the pattern guarantees \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) uniformly for all admissible \(D\in\mathcal D\), all \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\), and every positive-semidefinite assignment to the \(c\) replacement slots if and only if, for every \(k<\ell\), \(\max\{n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{10}^{k\ell},n_{00}^{k\ell}+n_{01}^{k\ell},n_{00}^{k\ell}+\mathbf 1\{n_{11}^{k\ell}>0\},\min(2,h)\}<h-c\). Failure of this inequality has an ambiguity witness with positive-definite invariant noise and positive-definite covariance slots; it is not a claim that every fixed singular boundary instance is ambiguous. In particular, any uniformly robustly identifying support pattern satisfies \(m\ge2c+3\), and this environment-count lower bound is attained by support patterns with no larger forced affine incidence.
statements.justification: The exact four-term formula turns a support hypergraph into a uniform published-class design threshold and exposes the unavoidable \(2c+3\) environment floor.
statements.gap: Existing generic-amplitude and sparse-shift results do not compute affine-line occupancy under whole-environment replacement or distinguish uniform class necessity from pointwise behavior at singular invariant-noise boundaries.
statements.consumer: Experimental planners can select intervention targets so the realized sparse design tolerates a prespecified number of arbitrary positive-semidefinite failed environments uniformly over the published second-moment class.

statements.statement: The set-theoretic simultaneous-coverage implication for arbitrary nonempty positive-semidefinite covariance regions is established by \(\text{thm:confidence-union-coverage}\). The result \(\text{thm:non-effective-four-margin-contraction}\) establishes a non-effective existential local radius and an explicit linear modulus under four bounds on the true instance---affine separation, normalization slack, structural conditioning, and scale---and only a condition-number bound on every feasible candidate. Can one additionally build and formally verify an executable real-closed-field quantifier-elimination, sign-determination, and root-isolation substrate which, from finite rational-semialgebraic covariance-region codes, (i) terminates and emits a quantifier-free code whose realization is exactly \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\), (ii) decides a release-or-abstain condition, possibly using a conservative universal four-margin audit to certify unknown true-side margins and forcing abstention within that audit whenever it finds a feasible candidate with zero affine separation, while distinguishing that operational sufficient audit from the sole candidate-side condition-number bound required by the analytic contraction theorem, (iii) decides for every rational population covariance family whether \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\) is empty, is a singleton, or contains at least two matrices, and (iv) computes a certified positive lower bound for the compact far-family residual and hence an effective positive radius \(r_0\)? Can the same verified program automate normalization-chart changes without altering the represented matrix set and support a corruption-aware extension of the CRAN \(\texttt{backShift}\) workflow? Every executable, effective, decision, chart-automation, and software item in this question is unresolved future work. A feasible candidate with zero affine separation or a small normalization slack may trigger that conservative operational audit, but neither is an analytic candidate-side obstruction to contraction around a fixed true instance satisfying \(\gamma_H\geq\gamma_0>0\) and \(\zeta_D\geq\zeta_0>0\).
statements.justification: Positive-semidefinite set-theoretic coverage and non-effective contraction under four true-side margins and only candidate conditioning are established. The remaining question is a formally verified executable algebraic and software interface.
statements.gap: Every code-generation, exact-decision, effective-radius, normalization-chart automation, release-or-abstain, and CRAN implementation item remains unresolved. A universal four-margin audit is only a possible conservative operational certificate; analytically, feasible candidates require only the condition-number bound.
statements.consumer: A future corruption-aware implementation must solve this question before claiming terminating exact inversion, certified release-or-abstain behavior, rational empty/singleton/multiple classification, chart automation, or an effectively computed local radius.

sampling_model.design: There are \(m\) labeled environments; an unknown set \(H\) of size \(h=m-c\) follows one population BACKSHIFT covariance model and the remaining \(c\) slots are arbitrary elements of \(\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\).
sampling_model.units: For population identification only \(\Sigma_e\) is observed. At each index \(n\), every slot supplies an independent within-environment sample of size \(n\) used to construct the indexed simultaneous covariance region \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Unknown additive shift interventions have diagonal covariance \(\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\); intervention targets and strengths are not observed.
sampling_model.overlap: The two candidate honest subsets may overlap in only \(m-2c=h-c\) slots.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance is estimated for the population theorem. Compatibility permits an invariant nuisance in \(\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\); the sharp converse and conditioning analysis impose the explicit interior condition \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\). The inference layer propagates indexed honest-slot simultaneous covariance regions through feasibility-oracle constraint inversion and measures all perturbations in operator norm.

estimand_functional: For a fixed honest design \(D,H,s\) and \(\Sigma\in(\mathbb S_+^p)^E\), let robust recovery mean that \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) for every positive-semidefinite assignment to the \(c\) slots in \(E\setminus H\). For every \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\), \(\delta_H>c\) implies robust recovery without an invertibility condition on the honest covariances. If the fixed instance has \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\), robust recovery holds if and only if \(\delta_H>c\), and failure is realized by positive-definite replacements. Thus \(\delta_H>c\) is minimax sharp over the published positive-semidefinite covariance and invariant-noise class, with failure witnessed in its positive-definite subclass.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The population BACKSHIFT solution is unique exactly when every pair of intervention-variance profiles is noncollinear.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The all-honest case of \(\text{thm:sharp-replacement-radius}\), with its affine rather than origin-based formulation after the invariant nuisance is removed by differencing.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: An exact non-unitary joint diagonalizer is essentially unique if and only if the diagonal-profile collinearity modulus is below one.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The results \(\text{lem:overlap-uniqueness}\) and \(\text{thm:sharp-replacement-radius}\) adapt complete-family uniqueness to competing honest subsets under BACKSHIFT normalization.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Outlier target matrices are omitted by iteratively retaining matrices whose geometric residual is below a chosen threshold.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The theorem \(\text{thm:sharp-replacement-radius}\) gives an exact worst-case whole-slot replacement threshold without selecting a residual trimming level.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives noiseless unique topology identification when the exogenous-covariance factor has Kruskal rank at least two, nonzero edges are continuously distributed, and at least two off-diagonal nonzero entries are known in every column.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The theorem \(\text{thm:sharp-replacement-radius}\) treats unknown whole-environment replacements, a common positive-semidefinite nuisance, nonnegative raw shifts, and the standard BACKSHIFT normalization rather than sparse within-matrix outliers or known edges.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Simultaneous diagonalizability by congruence of a complete Hermitian family is equivalent to positive-definite feasibility of a linear matrix system.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The definition \(\text{def:subset-consensus}\) records only finite enumeration to a full-solution feasibility oracle; executable projection and exact union generation remain in \(\text{oeq:certified-uniform-inference}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Pairwise environment comparisons identify causal structure with high probability under probabilistically sparse mechanism changes.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The results \(\text{prop:generic-support-frontier}\) and \(\text{prop:uniform-support-deletion-radius}\) give the exact four-term affine-incidence frontier and the exact worst-deletion threshold for a prespecified support array.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The randomized SDC algorithm exactly diagonalizes an exactly SDC complete symmetric family with probability one and, under its regularity condition, achieves high-probability \(\mathcal O(\varepsilon)\) diagonalization error when every member of the family is within \(\varepsilon\) of an SDC family.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The theorem \(\text{thm:sharp-replacement-radius}\) treats adversarial replacement of \(c\) whole environments and competing size-\(h\) subsets, while \(\text{thm:non-effective-four-margin-contraction}\) gives an existential local modulus for the full set-theoretic union under four true-side margins and only candidate conditioning; neither result claims a randomized complete-family algorithm.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Local perturbation sensitivity for an already selected approximate joint diagonalization problem is controlled by its uniqueness and conditioning quantities.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The theorem \(\text{thm:non-effective-four-margin-contraction}\) handles competing size-\(h\) subsets through a global compact residual gap followed by local affine-minor inversion. Its four affine-separation, normalization-slack, conditioning, and scale margins are true-side conditions; its feasible-candidate premise retains only conditioning, and its radius is existential.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Identification-robust tests and confidence sets maintain uniform asymptotic size across weak and strong identification regimes.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The theorem \(\text{thm:confidence-union-coverage}\) is a finite-sample set-theoretic inversion implication for arbitrary supplied positive-semidefinite covariance regions, and \(\text{thm:non-effective-four-margin-contraction}\) is a local result under fixed positive true-side margins and only candidate conditioning; neither is a generic weak-identification inference procedure.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The current CRAN \(\texttt{backShift}\) workflow estimates cyclic linear structure from heterogeneous covariance information.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: No software claim is matched: a corruption-aware extension, executable feasibility, certified release-or-abstain behavior, and an effective radius remain exclusively in \(\text{oeq:certified-uniform-inference}\).

tldr: Unknown shift interventions identify a cyclic linear causal system because covariance differences share a non-unitary congruence diagonalizer. The field-tier kernel asks how many entire covariance environments may instead be arbitrary. The structural matrix satisfying the BACKSHIFT unit-diagonal and cycle-product normalization survives every \(c\)-slot positive-definite replacement if and only if deleting the largest affine-line subset from every pairwise honest shift cloud costs more than \(c\) environments. The converse uses the explicit interior condition on invariant noise to produce a legal positive-definite contamination and a second cycle-product-normalized system. A generic sparse-support formula turns the distance into a combinatorial design criterion; finite subset enumeration is only a reduction to an exact feasibility oracle, while operator-norm contraction of indexed confidence unions, rational certificates, and mandatory abstention at zero affine separation remain the computational agenda for updating the CRAN pooled-difference workflow.

project_justification.gap: Published BACKSHIFT identifies from an entirely honest environment family, general joint-diagonalization theory studies one complete matrix family, and existing outlier-aware joint diagonalization uses a tuning threshold without an exact adversarial radius.
project_justification.niche: Whole-environment replacement creates a discrete overlap geometry: two explanations may discard different slots and therefore share only \(m-2c\) covariance matrices. Affine rather than linear collinearity is the invariant obstruction because the common nondiagonal noise covariance disappears only after differencing.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the necessary-and-sufficient distance \(\delta_H>c\), a matching positive-definite contamination witness satisfying the BACKSHIFT cycle-product normalization under the interior-noise condition, and the exact generic support-incidence formula. Finite subset enumeration is recorded only as a definitional feasibility-oracle implementation note. The open inference target asks for explicit operator-norm radius and modulus functions for indexed confidence unions on fixed-margin uniform classes, rational certificates, chart switching, and abstention at vanishing affine minors.

related_work: The field-tier radius result is informed by RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Theorem 1 and its appendix proof, which supplies the all-honest model, pairwise profile reduction, and cycle-product normalization; its generic-amplitude result is Corollary 2(ii). KleinsteuberShen2013NUJDUniqueness, Theorem 1, informs the complete-family uniqueness step through profile collinearity. AkhavanEtAl2019GeometryJD, Section 4.2 and equation (42), informs the robust joint-diagonalization setting by trimming outlier target matrices with a chosen residual threshold, but it does not state a worst-case replacement radius. ShenEtAl2020RJDSEM, Section III.C and equations (27)--(28), defines R-JDSEM through an elementwise \(\ell_1\) joint-diagonalization loss for sparse node- or entry-level outlier components within local covariance matrices, rather than replacement of whole covariance slabs. Its noiseless anchored or known-edge Theorem 1 establishes a sufficient uniqueness result under prior edge information; it gives neither an adversarial whole-environment replacement radius, the criterion \(\delta_H>c\), nor a legal two-explanation BACKSHIFT converse. PerryVonKugelgenScholkopf2022SparseShift, Corollary 4.2, Theorem 5.3, and Corollary 5.4, shows how pairwise environment comparisons and sparse mechanism changes support detection and graph recovery, while PfisterPeters2022SparseIV, Theorem 3, illustrates how a support pattern can control generic causal identifiability. LeNguyen2022HermitianSDC, Theorem 7 and Algorithm 5, supplies a complete-family congruence-feasibility primitive; this proposal uses it only to motivate an oracle reduction and does not claim a terminating exact solver. Afsari2008JDSensitivity relates local joint-diagonalization error to conditioning and a uniqueness modulus. AndrewsCheng2013SporadicID motivates confidence procedures that remain valid as identification disappears. None of these sources characterizes adversarial positive-definite replacement of covariance environments under BACKSHIFT normalization and nonnegative raw shifts.

honest_scope: The exact population radius and generic sparse-support frontier are theorem targets. The invariant nuisance is positive semidefinite in the standard BACKSHIFT layer and is required to be positive definite only for the sharp converse, the raw-covariance \(c=0\) reduction, and conditioning claims. Finite subset enumeration is a definitional reduction to a full-solution feasibility oracle, not an encoded solver. The rational certificate atlas, implementable feasibility routine, normalization-chart switching, and operator-norm contraction of \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}\) remain the first-class open question. Contraction is requested only along indexed region sequences with \(r_{n,\alpha,H}\to0\), uniformly on classes bounded away from zero affine separation, normalization slack, and positive-definiteness margins and bounded above in condition number and scale; at \(\gamma_H=0\), set-valued output or abstention remains mandatory. At \(c=0\), the positive-definite raw-covariance criterion is explicitly a non-novel reduction to the published BACKSHIFT noncollinearity result; no statistical rate is claimed without explicit covariance-region inputs.
